subject.title: [Feature]: Fallback approval mode + model attribution in messages

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off approval gate before executing configured model fallbacks, and what should the config, timeout, denial, and delivery semantics be?
rationale: The remaining request adds provider-routing control and config surface in a fallback hot path; repository policy treats fallback behavior and config/default additions as compatibility- and product-sensitive.

options.title: Design a core opt-in fallback gate
options.body: Define a per-agent or per-run approval contract with timeout behavior, channel delivery, docs, and tests before implementing the runtime pause.

options.title: Keep fallback automatic
options.body: Treat response-prefix attribution and fallback notices/logs as the supported visibility model and close the approval-gate direction as not planned.

options.title: Route through extension/API design
options.body: Design a generic approval or fallback-decision extension hook first instead of adding a one-off model config key.

recommendation.title: Design a core opt-in fallback gate
recommendation.body: Define a per-agent or per-run approval contract with timeout behavior, channel delivery, docs, and tests before implementing the runtime pause.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history route spans model fallback policy, config-sensitive fallback behavior, and reply-prefix context.
